detail.body:
## Purpose

> **Update (2026-10-13), per review from @njhill and @hickeyma:** the fast path is now a public engine-level flag, `SamplingParams.sampled_logprobs_only`, so `LLM` / `AsyncLLM` callers (e.g. RL frameworks such as verl that call `AsyncLLM.generate()` directly) get the same speedup. `GenerateRequest.return_token_logprobs` and the `logprobs > 0` "both" mode are removed, the `--logprobs-mode` check moved to engine-level validation, and `/inference/v1/generate` now also supports it when streaming. The engine transport and output-processor path measured below are unchanged. The live-server tests below have not been rerun on a GPU since this change (no GPU available to me right now); the unit tests, an in-process run of the non-streaming and streaming response paths with the real router and exception handlers, and the Rust crates pass locally.

RL rollout collectors need one float per generated token: the sampled token's logprob. Today that means requesting `logprobs=0` and reading `logprobs[i][token_id].logprob` (engine API) or `choices[].logprobs.content[i].logprob` (`/inference/v1/generate`). On the server, that one float travels a path built for top-k logprob objects: the scheduler slices a `LogprobsLists` (token ids, logprobs, ranks — three numpy arrays) per request per step, encodes it into `EngineCoreOutput`, the output processor `.tolist()`s it, detokenizes every entry and appends `Logprob` objects (or `FlatLogprobs`), and the frontend builds a Pydantic object per token before JSON.

Measured on one L20 with an 8-core host (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, 256-token rollouts with `ignore_eos`, prompts = 2 × concurrency, `temperature=1, top_k=50, top_p=0.95`), `logprobs=0` takes throughput to **0.67–0.73× of no-logprobs** at concurrency 64–512. Where the cost sits, established by switching layers off one at a time (raw runs linked below): the GPU kernels are not it (skipping `_ranks_kernel` is within noise; skipping every logprob kernel is worth ≤5 points); the D2H copy and `tolists()` are free; the per-request `LogprobsLists` slicing → IPC → output-processor → Pydantic path is the whole cost (skipping the slicing alone restores 1.00× at c256).

This PR adds a sampled-token logprob fast path, end to end:

- **Engine API:** `SamplingParams.sampled_logprobs_only: bool = False`. It implies `logprobs=0` when `logprobs` is unset; any other `logprobs` value and `logprob_token_ids` are rejected (`VLLMValidationError`). The values come back as `CompletionOutput.sampled_logprobs: list[float]` (unclamped), `CompletionOutput.logprobs` is `None`, and `cumulative_logprob` is still computed. Works with `n > 1`, DELTA outputs (`RequestOutput.add` merges them) and speculative decoding.
- **Validation:** requires `--logprobs-mode raw_logprobs` or `processed_logprobs`, checked in `SamplingParams._validate_logprobs`, so `AsyncLLM` callers get it too (the values are named logprobs; logits are not handed back under that name).
- **Scheduler:** emits `EngineCoreOutput.new_sampled_logprobs`, one float per new token, read from column 0 of the step's logprobs array (the sampler stores the sampled token first), through the `cu_num_generated_tokens` boundaries. No `LogprobsLists` for these requests.
- **Output processor:** keeps a plain float list and the cumulative logprob; it never builds `Logprob` entries and never detokenizes.
- **`/inference/v1/generate`:** reads the flag from `sampling_params`. Each choice carries `logprobs.sampled: list[float]` (`GenerateLogProbs.sampled`, per chunk when streaming), clamped like `content` (`-inf` and NaN become `-9999.0`), with `content: null`. `sampled` is omitted from responses that did not ask for it, so the existing schema is unchanged. `output_mode="text"` is rejected (400): text mode returns `ChatCompletionLogProbs`, which has no `sampled`.
- **Rust frontend:** rejects `sampling_params.sampled_logprobs_only=true` explicitly (`invalid_request_error`) instead of silently dropping it; the Rust engine-core client mirrors the new last-appended `EngineCoreOutput` field.

It composes with `--return-sampling-mask` (#54901): the rollout contract "mask + sampled-token logprob" is then one ragged list and one flat list per request.

## Test Plan

- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py -k sampled` (live server): flat array equals the `logprobs=0` object path's per-token `logprob`, with `logprobs` unset and `logprobs=0` (greedy; and under n-gram speculative decoding, where steps produce a ragged number of tokens per request, on a `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` server — without batch-invariant execution the object path was not a stable numerical oracle in that configuration); `n=2` / `n=4` return one aligned array per choice; streaming chunks carry their own values and join to the non-streaming array; `logprobs=2`, `logprobs=-1`, `logprob_token_ids` → 400; `output_mode="text"` → 400; `--logprobs-mode raw_logits` → 400; `sampled` absent unless requested (non-streaming and streaming).
- `tests/v1/test_outputs.py`: column-0 selection with and without `cu_num_generated_tokens`, including the ragged `[0, 3, 4, 6]` case, and DELTA merging in `RequestOutput.add`. `tests/v1/engine/test_logprobs_processor.py`: float-list accumulation and cumulative logprob; `SamplingParams` defaults and rejections; the `--logprobs-mode` check for all four modes; the flag set through the `/inference/v1/generate` request schema survives msgpack to the engine.
- Rust: `cargo test -p vllm-server` (incl. the new rejection test) and `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client` (round-trip of the new output field).
- Exactness under sampling: one server with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and `--return-sampling-mask`, 16 seeded prompts × 64 tokens, each sent once as `logprobs=0` (objects) and once with the fast path: token sequences identical 16/16, array length equals generated length 16/16, max abs difference 0.0.
- Serving A/B: one `vllm serve` per condition, 3 interleaved rounds, per-round API-server and EngineCore CPU from `/proc`.

## Test Result

vLLM 0.29.0 + #54901 backported, one L20, driver 580.159.04, `/inference/v1/generate`, non-streaming. "vs gen" is relative to the same server with no logprobs requested.

| Model | Concurrency | no logprobs | `logprobs=0` objects | `sampled_logprobs_only` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | 64 | 18,592 tok/s | 13,495 (0.73×) | **17,868 (0.96×)** |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | 256 | 23,038 | 15,451 (0.67×) | **21,846 (0.95×)** |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, `--return-sampling-mask` | 64 | 16,452 | 11,106 | **15,453 (0.94×)** |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B, `--return-sampling-mask` | 256 | 20,313 | 13,088 | **19,132 (0.94×)** |
| Qwen3-4B | 64 | 3,524 | 3,351 (0.95×) | **3,503 (0.99×)** |
| Qwen3-4B, `--return-sampling-mask` | 64 | 3,442 | 3,320 | **3,443 (1.00×)** |

On the 0.5B model the flag recovers ~84–86% of the throughput that `logprobs=0` costs; response size per request goes from ~41 KB to ~6.8 KB; API-server CPU with logprobs returns to the no-logprobs level (0.39 vs 0.37 of a core at c256) and the EngineCore is at parity. On the GPU-bound 4B model the sampled-token logprob becomes essentially free.

Raw runs, the layer-by-layer decomposition, and the exactness check: <https://github.com/yinli-systems/single-gpu-inference-lab/tree/stage2-compact-sampling-mask/benchmarks/results/l20-flat-token-logprobs> and `.../l20-logprob-engine-decomposition`.

Related: #42259 (logprobs semantics RFC), #54901 (compact sampling masks), #48314 (RL roadmap: RL artifacts data plane). #42283 (FlatLogprobs tail slices) is orthogonal. The AuxOutput connector work (#45635) targets persistence/prefix reuse/external transfer of auxiliary outputs; this change stays on the request-local serving path and does not add a new artifact plane.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `token_in_token_out logprobs`, `flat logprobs`, `LogprobsProcessor`, `sampled logprobs` on 2026-09-18. #46422 (skip detokenization in beam search) and #55029 (streaming derender logprobs) touch adjacent code; neither changes the generate response shape or the engine-core transport.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
